evt.def: If $f$ is continuous on a closed interval $[a, b]$, then $f$ has at least one absolute maximum value and at least one absolute minimum value on $[a, b]$.

critical-point.def: An interior point $c$ of the domain of $f$ where $f'(c) = 0$ or $f'(c)$ does not exist. Relative extrema can occur only at critical points.

absolute-extremum.def: An absolute (global) maximum is a value $f(c)$ with $f(c) \ge f(x)$ for every $x$ in the domain or interval considered; an absolute minimum has $f(c) \le f(x)$ for every such $x$.

relative-extremum.def: A relative (local) maximum is a value $f(c)$ with $f(c) \ge f(x)$ for every $x$ in some open interval around $c$; a relative minimum has $f(c) \le f(x)$ there. It is a peak or valley compared with nearby points only.
